Yasser Arafat: President of Palestine from 1989 to 2004.

Álvaro Uribe: President of Colombia from 2002 to 2010.
Which of these people was born first?
Jabir ibn Hayyan (born 721) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these people was born first?
Omar Khayyam (born 1048) is the earliest of the four.
Fortran (founded 1957) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is the oldest?
Python (programming language) (founded 1991) is the earliest of the four.
Pick the astronomer from these four.
Galileo Galilei is an astronomer. Galileo has been called the father of observational astronomy, modern-era classical physics, the scientific method, and modern science.
Who among these is a mathematician?
Carl Friedrich Gauss is a mathematician. Gauss was director of the Göttingen Observatory in Germany and professor of astronomy from 1807 until his death in 1855.
What is the atomic number of Seaborgium?
Seaborgium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Sg and atomic number 106.
What is the atomic number of Bromine?
Bromine is a chemical element; it has symbol Br and atomic number 35.
In what year did Galileo Galilei die?
Galileo Galilei: Galileo has been called the father of observational astronomy, modern-era classical physics, the scientific method, and modern science.
In what year was Lithium discovered?
Lithium (from Ancient Greek: λίθος, líthos, 'stone') is a chemical element; it has symbol Li and atomic number 3.
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-23: Russian Aircraft Corporation MiG. It is a third-generation jet fighter, alongside similar Soviet aircraft such as the Su-17 "Fitter".
Which country is Dassault Falcon 900 from?
Dassault Falcon 900: France. The Dassault Falcon 900, commonly abbreviated as the F900, is a French-built corporate trijet aircraft made by Dassault Aviation.
Which country is Yakovlev MC-21 based from?
Yakovlev MC-21: Russia. The aircraft made its maiden flight on 28 May 2017 from Irkutsk.
Who is credited with discovering Livermorium?
Livermorium: Joint Institute for Nuclear Research. Livermorium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Lv and atomic number 116.
Who is credited with discovering Fentanyl?
Fentanyl: Paul Janssen. Fentanyl is a highly potent synthetic opioid of the piperidine family, used primarily as pain medication.
Who is credited with discovering Arsenic?
Arsenic: Albertus Magnus. Arsenic is a chemical element; it has the symbol As and atomic number 33.
A King's College Cambridge graduate who earned a Princeton doctorate in 1938, he later joined Britain's wartime codebreaking effort and pioneered theoretical computing — who was he?
Alan Turing (23 June 1912 - 7 June 1954) was an English mathematician, computer scientist, logician, cryptanalyst, philosopher and theoretical biologist.
Despite overseeing Soviet thermonuclear weapons development, this physicist won the 1975 Nobel Peace Prize for his activism on human rights and individual freedom — who is he?
Andrei Sakharov (21 May 1921 - 14 December 1989) was a Soviet physicist and a Nobel Peace Prize laureate, which he was awarded in 1975 for emphasizing human rights around the world.
Which noble gas, symbol Ar and atomic number 18, is the third most abundant gas in Earth's atmosphere — more plentiful there than carbon dioxide or neon?
Argon is a chemical element; it has symbol Ar and atomic number 18.
Only eight species of this stocky-legged, shaggy, short-tailed carnivoran survive, ranging across North and South America and Eurasia — what mammal is it?
Bear are carnivoran mammals of the family Ursidae.

This general medical term describes blood escaping a damaged vessel, whether internally or through a puncture in the skin, with the loss of more than about 15 percent of total volume proving potentially fatal. What is it called?
Bleeding is blood escaping from the circulatory system from damaged blood vessels.

Naturally green and yellow with scalloped black markings, this small, long-tailed seed-eating parrot native to Australia is bred worldwide in colors from blue to white — which bird, also called a budgie?
Budgerigar (--ree-; Melopsittacus undulatus), also known as the common parakeet, shell parakeet or budgie, is a small, long-tailed, seed-eating parrot native to Australia.

Born in London and raised in Milan, this Italian Catholic teenager taught himself computer programming and web design to promote devotion to the Eucharist online before his death in 2006 at age 15 — who was he?
Carlo Acutis (3 May 1991 - 12 October 2006) was an English-born Italian Catholic teenager known for his devotion to the Eucharist and his use of digital media to promote Catholic devotion.
This plant-cell organelle uses chlorophyll pigments to capture sunlight and convert it into chemical energy, ultimately producing sugar via the Calvin cycle — what is it?
Chloroplast (-plahst) is a type of organelle known as a plastid that conducts photosynthesis mostly in plant and algal cells.
A true thrush of Europe, western Asia and North Africa, the male of its nominate subspecies is entirely black — and depending on latitude it may stay put or migrate. What bird is it?
Common blackbird (Turdus merula) is a species of true thrush.

Named for a mythological Greek youth who was transformed into a tree after accidentally killing a beloved stag, this genus of evergreen conifers is considered polyphyletic by modern genetic analysis — what genus is it?
Cupressus (common name cypress) is one of several genera of evergreen conifers within the family Cupressaceae; for the others, see cypress.
Caused by a Corynebacterium bacterium, this infection can spin a tough grey 'pseudomembrane' across the throat that slowly chokes off the airway — what is it?
Diphtheria is an infection caused by the bacterium Corynebacterium diphtheriae. The pseudomembrane can grow to cover a wide area of the throat, leading to strangulation and death.
A onetime clerk for Justice Thurgood Marshall, this Harvard Law School dean was tapped for the Supreme Court by President Obama in 2010 — who is she?
Elena Kagan (born April 28, 1960) is an American lawyer who serves as an associate justice of the Supreme Court of the United States.
They're a tiny minority by headcount among living things, yet their larger bodies make their combined biomass dwarf that of bacteria and archaea — what membrane-bound-nucleus group is this?
Eukaryote are the domain Eukaryota or Eukarya, organisms whose cells have a membrane-bound nucleus.
Systematically named methanal and carrying the formula CH2O, this pungent gas turns up in particle board, disinfectants, and lab specimen jars — what is it?

Formaldehyde (for-, US also fr-) (systematic name methanal) is a pungent colorless gas mainly used in the production of industrial resins, such as for particle board, coatings, plastics, pulp, paper, synthetic fibers, and textiles.
The largest of four living anteater species, this terrestrial mammal of Central and South America is known for its elongated snout, bushy tail, and long foreclaws. What is it?
Giant anteater (Myrmecophaga tridactyla) is an insectivorous mammal native to Central and South America.
Named from Ancient Greek words for 'blood' and 'to make,' this biological process produces up to a hundred billion new blood cells per day in a healthy adult — what is it?
Haematopoiesis (from Ancient Greek (hama) 'blood' and (poien) 'to make'; also hematopoiesis in US English, sometimes h(a)emopoiesis) is the formation of blood cellular components.

Discovered in 2013 deep in South Africa's Rising Star Cave system, this archaic human left behind over 1,500 bones from at least 15 individuals, yet a tiny brain keeps its place in our family tree a puzzle — what species is it?

Homo naledi is an extinct species of archaic human discovered in 2013 in the Rising Star Cave system, Gauteng province, South Africa, part of the Cradle of Humankind, dating back to the Middle Pleistocene 335,000-236,000 years ago.

A leading figure among Israel's 'New Historians,' this scholar characterizes the 1948 Palestinian expulsion as a deliberate campaign in his research and now teaches at the University of Exeter — who is he?
Ilan Pappé (born 7 November 1954) is an Israeli historian and political scientist, known for his work on the Israeli-Palestinian conflict and as a leading figure among the New Historians.
Most of the flowers used by the global perfume industry for this fragrant genus of shrubs and vines are grown in a single Egyptian village. What plant is it?
Jasmine (botanical name: Jasminum) is a genus of shrubs and vines in the olive family of Oleaceae.

This childhood illness of unknown cause mainly affects kids under five, causing a prolonged fever lasting more than five days that doesn't respond to typical fever-reducing medicine, plus inflamed blood vessels throughout the body — name the syndrome?
Kawasaki disease (also known as mucocutaneous lymph node syndrome) is a syndrome of unknown cause that results in a fever and mainly affects children under 5 years of age.
Its pale golden coat is patterned not with simple dots but with dark spots clustered into rings called rosettes, and it has prowled Africa and Asia since the Early Pleistocene — which big cat is it?
Leopard (Panthera pardus) is one of the five extant cat species in the genus Panthera.
Named for their strong, monogamous pair bonding and the long stretches paired birds spend sitting together, this small genus of African parrots is popular as a pet — what is it commonly called?
Lovebird is the common name for the genus Agapornis, a small group of parrots in the Old World parrot family Psittaculidae.
Covering everything from B2B deals to a government's 'Got Milk?'-style campaigns, this business pillar means acquiring, satisfying and retaining customers — what is this discipline called?
Marketing is the act of acquiring, satisfying and retaining customers. It is one of the primary components of business management and commerce.
This Cuban engineer-turned-politician became his country's top leader in 2021, making him the first head of Cuba since the 1959 revolution who isn't a member of the Castro family — who is he?

Miguel Díaz-Canel (Latin American; born 20 April 1960) is a Cuban politician and engineer who has served as the 8th First Secretary of the Communist Party of Cuba and the top leader of Cuba since 2021.

Chemically known as bis(2-chloroethyl) sulfide, this organosulfur compound is a potent alkylating agent and carcinogen with no preventive antidote — protection relies entirely on covering the skin and airways. Name this notorious chemical warfare agent?
Mustard gas are names commonly used for the organosulfur chemical compound bis(2-chloroethyl) sulfide, which has the chemical structure S(CH2CH2Cl)2, as well as other species.
Catalyzed in nature by iron-bearing nitrogenase enzymes and famously partnered with legumes, this process turns molecular N2 into ammonia — what's it called?
Nitrogen fixation is a chemical process by which molecular dinitrogen (N2) is converted into ammonia (NH3).

This group of middle-ear inflammations includes a painful acute infection that makes young children tug at their ears, plus a quieter form defined by non-infectious fluid lingering for weeks. What is the condition?
Otitis media is a group of inflammatory diseases of the middle ear.
Built for the sea, it sports a spiny tongue and powerful jaws to grip slippery fish, then swallows them whole mid-swim. Which animal splits its life half on land, half in the water?
Penguin are a group of flightless semi-aquatic sea birds which live almost exclusively in the Southern Hemisphere.
Native to South America and the most economically important member of the Bromeliaceae family, this tropical 'multiple fruit' became a 17th-century European symbol of luxury — what is it?
Pineapple (Ananas comosus) is a tropical plant with an edible fruit; it is the most economically significant plant in the family Bromeliaceae.

This corticosteroid drug treats a huge range of conditions — from rheumatoid arthritis and asthma to eye inflammation and certain cancers — and can be taken orally, injected, or applied to the skin. What is it?
Prednisolone is a corticosteroid, a steroid hormone used to treat certain types of allergies, inflammatory conditions, autoimmune disorders, and cancers, electrolyte imbalances, and skin conditions.
This root vegetable in the mustard family, whose entire plant (leaves included) is edible, was domesticated in Asia and is now grown worldwide — what vegetable is it?
Radish (Raphanus sativus or Raphanus raphanistrum subsp.
This big, sociable black corvid is told apart from its relatives by a bare, whitish patch on its face, and it nests in noisy treetop colonies near farms and villages — which bird is it?
Rook (bird) (Corvus frugilegus) is a member of the family Corvidae in the passerine order of birds.

These colorful predatory marine animals — single polyps usually anchored by their base — are named after a terrestrial flower and, unlike their jellyfish relatives, skip the medusa stage entirely; what are they?
Sea anemone (-) are a group of predatory marine invertebrate animals constituting the order Actiniaria.
Unlike its shelled cousin the snail, this soft-bodied land mollusk gets by with no shell at all, or at most a tiny internal remnant of one — what animal is it?
Slug is a common name for any apparently shell-less terrestrial gastropod mollusc.
Built from four fused rings, compounds in this class include cholesterol, testosterone, and anti-inflammatory drugs like dexamethasone. What class of compound is it?
Steroid is an organic compound with four fused rings (designated A, B, C, and D) arranged in a specific molecular configuration.
Every part of this Old World evergreen tree is poisonous except the fleshy red covering around its seed, and it's native across Eurasia and Northwest Africa — what tree species is it?
Taxus baccata is an Old World species of evergreen tree in the family Taxaceae.

A colorless, sweet-smelling liquid that helps give gasoline and paint fumes their aroma, this benzene relative — a methyl group on a phenyl ring — serves as paint thinner and industrial solvent. What is it?
Toluene is a substituted aromatic hydrocarbon with the chemical formula C6H5CH3, often abbreviated as PhCH3, where Ph stands for the phenyl group.

This membrane-bound organelle, found in plant and fungal cells and some others, is essentially a water-filled storage compartment with no fixed shape, formed when smaller membrane vesicles fuse together. What is it called?
Vacuole is a membrane-bound organelle which is present in plant and fungal cells and some protist, animal, and bacterial cells.
This American child prodigy, son of a prominent psychiatrist, lectured on four-dimensional geometry at age 12 and graduated from Harvard cum laude at 16. Who was he?

William James Sidis (April 1, 1898 - July 17, 1944) was an American child prodigy whose exceptional abilities in mathematics and languages made him one of the most famous intellectual prodigies of the early 20th century.
The first Muslim scientist to win a Nobel Prize, this Pakistani theoretical physicist shared the 1979 Physics prize for unifying the weak and electromagnetic forces — who was he?
First flown in October 1972, this was the world's first twin-engine wide-body airliner, born from a 1967 France-West Germany-UK collaboration that later lost its British partner — what is it?
Airbus A300: World's first twin-engine widebody jet airliner.
This three-star system includes Proxima, the closest star to the Sun, and shines as the third-brightest point in the night sky after Sirius and Canopus — which system?
Alpha Centauri: Star system in the Centaurus constellation.
Commonly called windflowers, which genus of the buttercup family is native to every continent except Australia, New Zealand, and Antarctica?
Anemone: Genus of flowering plants in the family Ranunculaceae.
This genus of orb-weaving spiders, encompassing the European garden spider and the barn spider among its 500-plus species, was named by an 18th-century Swedish naturalist in 1757 — which genus?
Araneus: Genus of spiders. The genus was erected by Carl Alexander Clerck in 1757.

Steel-blue with wavy black markings on its back and silvery underneath, this shoaling fish thrives in the cooler waters of the Mediterranean, Black Sea, and northern ocean near Europe — which species?
Atlantic mackerel: Species of fish. The Atlantic mackerel's body is elongate, steel-blue marked with wavy black lines dorsally and silvery-white ventrally, its snout long and pointed.

This facial hair — most common among adult men, though it can also appear in women with a condition called hirsutism — has symbolized everything from wisdom and virility to poor hygiene across different cultures — what is it?
Beard: Hair on the chin, lower face and neck.
Made by combining phenol and acetone, this compound forms 65 to 70 percent of the world's polycarbonate plastics production — which chemical?
Bisphenol A: Chemical used in plastics, xenoestrogen.

Unlike most elements, this one is forged entirely by cosmic-ray spallation and supernovae rather than stellar fusion, and is mined from evaporite minerals like borax, mostly in Turkey — which element?
Boron: Chemical element with atomic number 5 (B)
Unlike benzodiazepines, this anti-anxiety medication doesn't cause sedation or dependence, and works through serotonin 5-HT1A receptors with a delayed onset of two to four weeks — which drug?
Buspirone: Medication used to treat anxiety disorders.
The largest living rodent, this semiaquatic South American grass-grazer lives in sociable herds of 10 to 20 — sometimes up to a hundred — near rivers and ponds; what is it?
A Turkish geologist honored by academies from the US to Russia to Serbia, he received the Gustav-Steinmann-Medaille, geology's top German prize. Who is he?
Celâl Şengör: Turkish scientist, geologist. Ali Mehmet Celâl Şengör (Turkish: [ˈali ˈmehmet ˈdʒeɫal ˈʃænɟœɾ]; born 24 March 1955) is a Turkish geologist.
A sweet-smelling, colorless solvent now made as a precursor to refrigerants and Teflon, this organochloride once served as an inhaled anesthetic from the 19th century onward — what is it?
Chloroform: CHCl3, historical anaesthetic and common solvent.
Many species of this venomous snake can rear up and flare a hood when threatened — what is it?
Cobra: Index of animals with the same common name.
This common bowel condition produces hard, infrequent stools and can lead to hemorrhoids or fecal impaction, with hypothyroidism and diabetes among its underlying causes. What is it?
Constipation: Infrequent or difficult bowel movements.
Native to the Irano-Turanian region, this flowering plant's dried seeds season cuisines worldwide, despite no strong evidence backing its use in traditional medicine — which spice?
Cumin: Species of plant with seeds used as a spice.
Often tied to diseases like Alzheimer's, this incurable, progressive syndrome erodes memory, language, and motivation in stages — which condition is being described?
Sold under the brand name Motilium, this dopamine-blocking medication treats nausea and slow stomach emptying, but also raises prolactin levels — what is it?
This American astronomer proved that many so-called nebulae were actually separate galaxies, and in 1929 showed that galaxies recede faster the farther away they are — who is he?
Triggered by the parasympathetic nervous system and a rise in nitric oxide, this physiological event leaves an organ firm and engorged — what is it?
Erection: Physiological phenomenon involving the hardening and enlargement of the penis.

Also known as the wisent, this species is the heaviest wild land mammal on its continent — hunted to extinction in the wild by the early 20th century before being restored through captive breeding programs. Which animal?
European bison: Eurasian species of mammal. It is one of two extant species of bison, alongside the American bison.
When fibroblasts overproduce collagen after repeated injury or chronic inflammation, this permanent connective-tissue scarring can impair an organ's normal function — what is it called?
Fibrosis: Excess connective tissue in healing.
Native from the British Isles east to the Caucasus, this tree in the olive family is prized for wood that's flexible, strong, and lightweight — what is its scientific name?
Fraxinus excelsior: Species of deciduous tree.
Called 'a bridge between the natural and social sciences,' this discipline studies Earth's lands, features, inhabitants, and how they all came to be — what is it?
Geography: Study of Earth's spatial information.
This common name covers edible fruit from the Ribes genus — the same genus as currants — coming in colors from green and red to purple, yellow, white, or black — which fruit?
Gooseberry: Species of Ribes cultivated for its edible fruit.
Producing up to a hundred billion new cells a day from specialized stem cells, this biological process manufactures every component of blood — what is it?
Haematopoiesis: Formation of blood cellular components.

Many people show no symptoms after catching this liver-attacking virus, but when signs do appear weeks later they can include nausea, yellowing skin, and fatigue — and an infection lasting past six months is deemed chronic. What is it?

Drawing on anthropology, paleontology and genetics, this field studies how our species gradually gained bipedalism, dexterity and complex language — and shows our past was weblike, with interbreeding among archaic humans — what is the subject?
Human evolution: Homo sapiens is a distinct species of the hominid family of primates, which includes all the great apes.

Named from the Greek word for "fish" because of its dry, scaly skin, this family of genetic skin disorders ranges from a mild type mistaken for ordinary dry skin to a rare, life-threatening form — which condition?
Ichthyosis: Family of disorders causing dry, thickened, scaly skin.

Native to the Americas but now grown worldwide, one species of this flowering plant genus has become such a popular ornamental that it's classified as an invasive weed on four continents — which genus?
Jacaranda: Genus of trees. The generic name is also used as the common name.

The id Software programmer behind Wolfenstein 3D, Doom, and Quake later left to become CTO of Oculus VR — before walking away again to chase artificial general intelligence. Which 3D-graphics wizard is he?
John Carmack: American computer programmer and video game developer (born 1970)
Marketed as Nizoral, this antifungal medication also treats Cushing's syndrome and excess hair growth in women, though oral use risks liver damage — which drug?
A genus of 47 flowering plant species in the sage family, prized for its fragrant oil and used in traditional medicine, cosmetics, and as a culinary herb across Mediterranean climates — which genus?
Lavandula: Genus of plants. Lavandula (common name lavender) is a genus of 47 known species of perennial flowering plants in the sage family, Lamiaceae.
Soft, movable, and painless, this benign fatty-tissue growth most often shows up under the skin on the upper back, shoulders, or abdomen — what is it?
Lipoma: Benign tumor made of fat tissue.
Native to China, Japan, Korea and Nepal and blooming in late summer after heavy rainfall, this plant's alternate names include the hurricane lily and the corpse flower — what is it?
Lycoris radiata: Species of plant. It is originally from China, Japan, Korea and Nepal and spread from there to the United States and elsewhere.
This American cultural anthropologist's 1928 fieldwork, Coming of Age in Samoa, made her a household name for exploring adolescence and sexuality in Pacific societies — who is she?
Typically occurring between ages 45 and 55, this natural decline in estrogen and progesterone permanently ends a woman's menstrual periods?
Menopause: Time when menstrual periods stop permanently.
Known to NATO as 'Flogger,' this Soviet variable-sweep-wing fighter was the first in the country's air force to carry look-down/shoot-down radar, with over 5,000 built. Which aircraft?
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-23: Soviet fighter-interceptor aircraft introduced in 1970.
Born in China and educated at MIT and Stanford, this billionaire engineer founded Taiwan's dominant chipmaker, serving as its CEO from 1987 to 2005 — who is he?
Morris Chang: Taiwanese businessman and electrical engineer (born 1931)

The males of this stocky Arctic cetacean sport a spiralled 'tusk' up to three metres long — actually a protruding left canine tooth thought to work as a weapon, a tool, and maybe a salinity sensor. What animal is it?
A catecholamine whose very name nods to the kidney, it acts as both a hormone and neurotransmitter and is called "noradrenaline" outside the US — what is it?
Norepinephrine: Catecholamine hormone and neurotransmitter. The general function of norepinephrine is to mobilize the brain and body for action.
Discovered by naturalist Alfred Russel Wallace in 1859, this fungus hijacks carpenter ants' brains and marches them down to the forest floor before killing them — which organism?

Ophiocordyceps unilateralis: Species of fungus. Ophiocordyceps unilateralis, commonly known as zombie-ant fungus, is an insect-pathogenic fungus, discovered by the British naturalist Alfred Russel Wallace in 1859.
First domesticated in Mesoamerica and led in production today by India, this tropical fruit belongs to the small genus Carica — what is it?
Papaya: Species of tropical fruit plant.
By learning to synthesize hormones from plant sterols — even wild Mexican yams — this research chemist laid the foundation for cortisone and the birth-control pill. Who was this pioneer?
Percy Lavon Julian: American research chemist (1899–1975)
Their name blends the Greek for "plant" and "drifter": these self-feeding plankton photosynthesize in the sunlit surface waters of oceans and lakes — what are they?
Phytoplankton: Autotrophic members of the plankton ecosystem.
Named from the Latin word for 'bridge' after Italian anatomist Costanzo Varolio, this brainstem structure sits above the medulla and below the midbrain — what is it?
Pons: Part of the brainstem in humans and other bipeds.

Marketed under brand names like Sudafed, this nasal decongestant can act as a stimulant and appetite suppressant at higher doses, making it both a medicine-cabinet staple and, at times, a drug of abuse. What is it?
Pseudoephedrine: Synthetic decongestant. Pseudoephedrine is a sympathomimetic medication which is used as a nasal decongestant to treat nasal congestion.
Nicknamed the 'stinking corpse lily,' this Southeast Asian plant genus produces the world's largest flower and was first seen by a Briton in 1818 after a local servant pointed it out — which genus?
This plant genus includes redcurrants, blackcurrants, and gooseberries, and also serves as the main alternate host for a fungal disease that attacks five-needle pines — which genus?
Ribes: Genus of flowering plants in the order Saxifragales.

Also called cot or crib death, this leading cause of infant mortality in the West strikes a baby under one, usually while sleeping between midnight and 9 a.m., and stays unexplained even after a full autopsy. What is it?
SIDS: Sudden unexplained death of a child who is less than one year of age.

Originally from the Mediterranean, this yellowish-gray arthropod has up to 15 pairs of long legs and preys on insects with venom too mild to harm humans — what species commonly invades homes worldwide?
Scutigera coleoptrata: Species of arthropod. Scutigera coleoptrata, also known as the house centipede, is a species of centipede that is typically yellowish-gray and has up to 15 pairs of long legs.
Named after a Native American war chief, this four-blade, twin-engine Army helicopter entered service in 1979 to replace the Bell UH-1 Iroquois — which aircraft is it?
Sikorsky UH-60 Black Hawk: Series of military utility transport helicopters.
Native to East Asia and the world's most-grown legume, this crop becomes everything from edamame and tofu to soy sauce, nattō and tempeh — what is it?
Soybean: Legume grown for its edible bean.
Named from Greek words for 'twisted' and 'grain,' this genus of spherical bacteria divides along a single axis to form chains, unlike its grape-cluster-forming cousins — coined in 1877, what is it?
Streptococcus: Genus of bacteria. In 1984, many bacteria formerly grouped in the genus Streptococcus were separated out into the genera Enterococcus and Lactococcus.
Marketed under the brand name Flomax, this alpha-blocker medication treats enlarged prostate symptoms and helps ease the passage of kidney stones — which drug?
Tamsulosin: Medication. Tamsulosin, sold under the brand name Flomax among others, is a medication used to treat symptomatic benign prostatic hyperplasia and chronic prostatitis.

Born from 19th-century efforts to make steam engines more efficient — thanks largely to French physicist Sadi Carnot — this branch of physics is governed by four fundamental laws relating heat, work, and energy. What is it?

Thermodynamics: Physics of heat, work, and temperature. The initial application of thermodynamics to mechanical heat engines was quickly extended to the study of chemical compounds and chemical reactions.

Famous for oversized, colorful bills nearly useless for excavation, these Neotropical birds nest in hollows dug by other animals and share an ecological niche with Africa and Asia's hornbills — what are they?
Toucan: Family of birds. The family includes five genera and over 40 different species.
Made from strained yogurt mixed with cucumber, garlic, and herbs like dill or mint, this cold Greek dip is a classic topping for souvlaki and gyros — what is it called?
Tzatziki: Cold cucumber–yogurt dip, soup, or sauce.

First glimpsed through Dmitri Ivanovsky's 1892 study of an ailing tobacco plant, this is the most numerous biological entity on Earth — yet it can only replicate inside another organism's living cells. What is it?
Virus: Infectious agent that replicates in cells.
This American child prodigy entered Harvard at 11 and lectured on four-dimensional geometry at 12 before deliberately retreating from public life — who was he?
William James Sidis: American mathematician, polyglot, and child prodigy (1898–1944)
Iron is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for iron is Fe. Iron is a chemical element; it has symbol Fe and atomic number 26.
Plutonium is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for plutonium is Pu. Plutonium is a chemical element; it has symbol Pu and atomic number 94.

Which one below is best known as a comedian?
Milton Berle is a comedian. Milton Berle (born Mendel Berlinger; Yiddish: ‏מענדעל בערלינגער; July 12, 1908 – March 27, 2002) was an American actor and comedian.
In what year was Russell Crowe born?
Russell Crowe: Russell Ira Crowe (born 7 April 1964) is a New Zealand–born actor and film director.
In what year was Ali Wong born?
Ali Wong: Alexandra Dawn Wong (born April 19, 1982) is an American actress and comedian.
In what year was Willem Dafoe born?
Willem Dafoe: William James "Willem" Dafoe ( də-FOH; born July 22, 1955) is an American actor.
In what year was Kris Kristofferson born?
Kris Kristofferson: Kristoffer Kristofferson (June 22, 1936 – September 28, 2024) was an American musician, songwriter, and actor.
